Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Sicoob.Sdk malicious NuGet package present on developer host (v2.0.0–2.0.4) · [LLM] Installation of vpmdhaj-published npm credential-stealer packages (14 known names) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] npm install lifecycle script reads AWS/Vault/CI credentials within minutes of package install · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound HTTPS or DNS to Sicoob/npm-cluster exfil domains (aab.sportsontheweb.net, oob.moika.tech) · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] PFX certificate read by .NET process followed by HTTPS egress to fake-Sentry domain · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] Sicoob.Sdk malicious NuGet package present on developer host (v2.0.0–2.0.4) Delivery High
Hunts for installation/restore of the trojanised Sicoob.Sdk NuGet package on developer or build hosts. The package is published under the actor profile 'sicoob' and any version in the 2.0.0–2.0.4 range is malicious — its SicoobClient class reads PFX certs from disk and exfiltrates them to a hardcoded fake-Sentry endpoint. Rationale: Hits the article's most specific IOC — package name 'Sicoob.Sdk' restricted to the exact malicious version range 2.0.0–2.0.4 published by Socket. No other version of this package exists in production NuGet today, so a file-shape match is enough to alert without behavioural correlation.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where (FolderPath has @"\.nuget\packages\sicoob.sdk\" or FolderPath has @"\packages\sicoob.sdk\" or FolderPath has @"/.nuget/packages/sicoob.sdk/")
| extend pkgVersion = extract(@"(?i)sicoob\.sdk[\\/](\d+\.\d+\.\d+)", 1, FolderPath)
| where pkgVersion in ("2.0.0","2.0.1","2.0.2","2.0.3","2.0.4")
| where FileName endswith ".dll" or FileName endswith ".nupkg" or FileName endswith ".nuspec"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, pkgVersion, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
| where TargetFilePath has @"\.nuget\packages\sicoob.sdk\" or TargetFilePath has @"\packages\sicoob.sdk\" or TargetFilePath has @"/.nuget/packages/sicoob.sdk/"
| extend pkgVersion = extract(@"(?i)sicoob\.sdk[\\/](\d+\.\d+\.\d+)", 1, TargetFilePath)
| where pkgVersion in ("2.0.0","2.0.1","2.0.2","2.0.3","2.0.4")
| where TargetFileExtension in~ ("dll","nupkg","nuspec")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, pkgVersion, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Malicious Sicoob.Sdk NuGet Package Installed (v2.0.0-2.0.4)
id: 2a3f1c0e-7d4e-4b18-9c1b-3e9c4a5d0f01
description: Detects file events under .nuget/packages/sicoob.sdk for the malicious 2.0.0-2.0.4 versions reported by Socket. Package exfiltrates PFX certs to aab.sportsontheweb.net.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/malicious-sicoob-nuget-steals-banking.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/29
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1036.005
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\.nuget\packages\sicoob.sdk\2.0.0\'
      - '\.nuget\packages\sicoob.sdk\2.0.1\'
      - '\.nuget\packages\sicoob.sdk\2.0.2\'
      - '\.nuget\packages\sicoob.sdk\2.0.3\'
      - '\.nuget\packages\sicoob.sdk\2.0.4\'
  selection_ext:

      - '.dll'
      - '.nupkg'
      - '.nuspec'

level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@TargetFilename:(*\\.nuget\\packages\\sicoob.sdk\\2.0.0\\* OR *\\.nuget\\packages\\sicoob.sdk\\2.0.1\\* OR *\\.nuget\\packages\\sicoob.sdk\\2.0.2\\* OR *\\.nuget\\packages\\sicoob.sdk\\2.0.3\\* OR *\\.nuget\\packages\\sicoob.sdk\\2.0.4\\* OR *\\.nuget\\packages\\Sicoob.Sdk\\2.0.0\\* OR *\\.nuget\\packages\\Sicoob.Sdk\\2.0.1\\* OR *\\.nuget\\packages\\Sicoob.Sdk\\2.0.2\\* OR *\\.nuget\\packages\\Sicoob.Sdk\\2.0.3\\* OR *\\.nuget\\packages\\Sicoob.Sdk\\2.0.4\\*))

| TargetFileName=/\\\.nuget\\packages\\sicoob\.sdk\\(2\.0\.[0-4])\\/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName], function=[count(), min(@timestamp), max(@timestamp)])

[LLM] PFX certificate read by .NET process followed by HTTPS egress to fake-Sentry domain Actions on Objectives High
Behavioural detection for the Sicoob.Sdk exfil chain: SicoobClient opens a .pfx file, base64-encodes it, and POSTs the bytes plus the client ID and PFX password to aab.sportsontheweb.net (a Sentry-impersonating domain). Correlates a PFX file event with an outbound network event by the same .NET process within 5 minutes. Rationale: Combines two article-specific signals: PFX file access by a .NET runtime (Sicoob SDK consumers are dotnet/csc/w3wp), and outbound to the named C2 domain aab.sportsontheweb.net, plus the sibling C2 oob.moika.tech for the parallel npm cluster. Same-process+5-minute correlation makes this very low-noise.
ATT&CKT1552.004 T1041 T1102
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let lookback = 30d;
let maxDelay = 5m;
let PfxReads = DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where FileName endswith ".pfx" or FileName endswith ".p12"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("dotnet.exe","w3wp.exe","csc.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","MSBuild.exe")
| project PfxTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, PfxPath=FolderPath, PfxFile=FileName;
let Egress = DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("sportsontheweb.net","moika.tech") or RemoteIP in ("")
| project NetTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, InitiatingProcessId, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort;
PfxReads
| join kind=inner Egress on DeviceId, InitiatingProcessId
| where NetTime between (PfxTime .. PfxTime + maxDelay)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', NetTime, PfxTime)
| project PfxTime, NetTime, DelaySec, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, PfxPath, PfxFile, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by PfxTime desc
let lookback = 30d;
let maxDelay = 5m;
let PfxReads = ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where TargetFileExtension in~ ("pfx","p12")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("dotnet.exe","w3wp.exe","csc.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","MSBuild.exe")
| project PfxTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActingProcessId, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername, PfxPath=TargetFilePath;
let Egress = ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where DstHostname has_any ("sportsontheweb.net","moika.tech") or Url has_any ("sportsontheweb.net","moika.tech")
| project NetTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActingProcessId=tostring(SrcPortNumber), DstHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber;
PfxReads
| join kind=inner Egress on DvcHostname
| where NetTime between (PfxTime .. PfxTime + maxDelay)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', NetTime, PfxTime)
| project PfxTime, NetTime, DelaySec, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, PfxPath, DstHostname, DstIpAddr
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*.pfx OR *.p12 OR *.PFX OR *.P12) @Image:(*\\dotnet.exe OR *\\w3wp.exe OR *\\csc.exe OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\Dotnet.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe)) OR (source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationHostname:(*sportsontheweb.net OR *moika.tech))
(#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo OR #event_simpleName=FileWritten) TargetFileName=/\.(pfx|p12)$/i ContextImageFileName=/(dotnet|w3wp|csc|powershell|pwsh|MSBuild)\.exe$/i

| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName, RemoteAddressIP4], function=count())

[LLM] npm install lifecycle script reads AWS/Vault/CI credentials within minutes of package install Installation High
Hunts the 'vpmdhaj' preinstall-hook chain plus the broader npm credential-harvester pattern. Looks for a node/npm/yarn/pnpm process touching ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.vault-token, ~/.npmrc, .env, or shell-history files within 10 minutes of an npm install kicking off — the exact behaviour Microsoft Defender Research called out for the 14 vpmdhaj packages. Rationale: Targets the exact behaviour Defender Research described for vpmdhaj's preinstall hooks (AWS keys, Vault tokens, npm tokens, CI secrets harvested from host environment), and also catches forge-jsxy and the 164-package oob.moika.tech cluster which share the same pattern. The 10-minute install-to-cred-read window cuts most legitimate dev-tool access to those files.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1059.007 T1546.016
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let lookback = 14d;
let maxDelay = 10m;
let Installs = DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where FileName in~ ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.cmd","pnpm.exe","node.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.cmd","pnpm.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (" install","preinstall","postinstall"," i "," ci "," add ") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (" install","preinstall","postinstall")
| project InstallTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InstallCmd=ProcessCommandLine;
let CredHits = DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
| where (FolderPath has @"\.aws\" or FolderPath has @"/.aws/"
      or FileName in~ (".vault-token",".npmrc",".env",".bash_history",".zsh_history")
      or FolderPath has @"\.vault" or FolderPath has @"/.vault"
      or FolderPath has @"\.docker\config" or FolderPath has @"/.docker/config"
      or FolderPath has @"\.kube\config" or FolderPath has @"/.kube/config")
| project CredTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, CredPath=FolderPath, CredFile=FileName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
Installs
| join kind=inner CredHits on DeviceId
| where CredTime between (InstallTime .. InstallTime + maxDelay)
| summarize CredFilesTouched=make_set(strcat(CredPath, CredFile), 25), FirstCred=min(CredTime), LastCred=max(CredTime), Cmd=any(InstallCmd) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InstallTime
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', FirstCred, InstallTime)
| order by InstallTime desc
let lookback = 14d;
let maxDelay = 10m;
let Installs = ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.cmd","pnpm.exe","node.exe") or ParentProcessName has_any ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (" install","preinstall","postinstall"," ci "," add ") or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any (" install","preinstall","postinstall")
| project InstallTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, InstallCmd=ActingProcessCommandLine;
let CredHits = ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
| where TargetFilePath has @"\.aws\" or TargetFilePath has @"/.aws/"
     or TargetFileName in~ (".vault-token",".npmrc",".env",".bash_history",".zsh_history")
     or TargetFilePath has @".vault"
     or TargetFilePath has ".docker/config" or TargetFilePath has ".kube/config"
| project CredTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, CredPath=TargetFilePath;
Installs
| join kind=inner CredHits on DvcHostname
| where CredTime between (InstallTime .. InstallTime + maxDelay)
| summarize CredFilesTouched=make_set(CredPath, 25), FirstCred=min(CredTime), Cmd=any(InstallCmd) by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, InstallTime
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', FirstCred, InstallTime)
| order by InstallTime desc
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\npm.cmd OR *\\npm.exe OR *\\yarn.exe OR *\\pnpm.exe OR *\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe) @CommandLine:(*preinstall* OR *postinstall* OR *"npm install"* OR *"npm ci"*)) OR (source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.parent.name:(npm OR node OR yarn OR pnpm) (@process.command_line:*preinstall* OR @process.command_line:*install*)) OR (source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe OR *\\npm.exe) @TargetFilename:(*\\.aws\\credentials* OR *\\.vault-token* OR *\\.npmrc* OR *\\.env OR *.docker\\config* OR *.kube\\config*))
(#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 OR #event_simpleName=SyntheticProcessRollup2) ImageFileName=/(node|npm|yarn|pnpm)(\.exe|\.cmd)?$/i CommandLine=/(preinstall|postinstall|\sinstall\b|\sci\b|\sadd\b)/i
| join({#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo OR #event_simpleName=FileWritten ContextImageFileName=/(node|npm|yarn|pnpm)(\.exe|\.cmd)?$/i TargetFileName=/(\.aws[\\\/]credentials|\.vault-token|\.npmrc$|[\\\/]\.env$|\.bash_history|\.zsh_history|\.docker[\\\/]config|\.kube[\\\/]config)/i}, field=[aid, ContextProcessId], include=[TargetFileName])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine], function=[count(), collect(TargetFileName)])

[LLM] Outbound HTTPS or DNS to Sicoob/npm-cluster exfil domains (aab.sportsontheweb.net, oob.moika.tech) Command & Control High
Pure IOC pivot on the two confirmed exfil domains from both campaigns — aab.sportsontheweb.net is the Sicoob.Sdk fake-Sentry endpoint, oob.moika.tech is the 164-npm-package /report beacon. Any developer, build, or CI host resolving or connecting to either domain is treated as compromised until proven otherwise. Rationale: Both domains are flagged in the article as hardcoded exfil endpoints (aab.sportsontheweb.net for Sicoob.Sdk's fake-Sentry POSTs, oob.moika.tech/report for the 164-npm-package env-var beacon). Neither is a legitimate corporate destination; any hit is high-fidelity. Wildcards on parent domains catch subdomain rotation by the actor.

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("638788afc4f1b5860a328312caf5895abd5f5632d28a4f2a85b09076e270d15d", "77d92efe7af3547f71fd41d4a884872d66b1be9499eaa637e91eac866911694d", "bfa149694ec6411c23936311a999163ade54d6f38e2f4b0e3cfb8cb67bd7cfaa") or SHA1 in~ ("638788afc4f1b5860a328312caf5895abd5f5632d28a4f2a85b09076e270d15d", "77d92efe7af3547f71fd41d4a884872d66b1be9499eaa637e91eac866911694d", "bfa149694ec6411c23936311a999163ade54d6f38e2f4b0e3cfb8cb67bd7cfaa") or MD5 in~ ("638788afc4f1b5860a328312caf5895abd5f5632d28a4f2a85b09076e270d15d", "77d92efe7af3547f71fd41d4a884872d66b1be9499eaa637e91eac866911694d", "bfa149694ec6411c23936311a999163ade54d6f38e2f4b0e3cfb8cb67bd7cfaa")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("638788afc4f1b5860a328312caf5895abd5f5632d28a4f2a85b09076e270d15d", "77d92efe7af3547f71fd41d4a884872d66b1be9499eaa637e91eac866911694d", "bfa149694ec6411c23936311a999163ade54d6f38e2f4b0e3cfb8cb67bd7cfaa") or SHA1 in~ ("638788afc4f1b5860a328312caf5895abd5f5632d28a4f2a85b09076e270d15d", "77d92efe7af3547f71fd41d4a884872d66b1be9499eaa637e91eac866911694d", "bfa149694ec6411c23936311a999163ade54d6f38e2f4b0e3cfb8cb67bd7cfaa") or MD5 in~ ("638788afc4f1b5860a328312caf5895abd5f5632d28a4f2a85b09076e270d15d", "77d92efe7af3547f71fd41d4a884872d66b1be9499eaa637e91eac866911694d", "bfa149694ec6411c23936311a999163ade54d6f38e2f4b0e3cfb8cb67bd7cfaa")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["638788afc4f1b5860a328312caf5895abd5f5632d28a4f2a85b09076e270d15d", "77d92efe7af3547f71fd41d4a884872d66b1be9499eaa637e91eac866911694d", "bfa149694ec6411c23936311a999163ade54d6f38e2f4b0e3cfb8cb67bd7cfaa"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).

[LLM] Web service in container spawning interactive shell (Redis/nginx RCE) Exploitation High
Hunts CVE-2025-49844 (Redis Lua RCE) and CVE-2026-24061 (nginx) post-exploitation pattern: redis-server, nginx, node or java spawning sh/bash/busybox inside a containerised host — the unambiguous fingerprint of RCE landing inside a vulnerable image. Rationale: Article names CVE-2025-49844 (Redis Lua RCE) and CVE-2026-24061 (nginx) as the in-container exploits driving Kinsing/perfctl/Dero/Mirai/Gafgyt staging. Cross-checked against MITRE T1190 page and abuse.ch ThreatFox notes on Kinsing post-exploit shell drop patterns. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/ • https://threatfox.abuse.ch/browse/malware/win.kinsing/
ATT&CKT1190 T1203 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("redis-server","nginx","node","java","httpd","apache2","php-fpm")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","busybox","ash","zsh")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("curl ","wget ","/tmp/","/dev/shm/","chmod +x","base64 -d","bash -i","|sh","|bash")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("redis-server","nginx","node","java","httpd","apache2","php-fpm")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("/sh","/bash","/dash","/busybox","/ash","/zsh")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("curl ","wget ","/tmp/","/dev/shm/","chmod +x","base64 -d","bash -i","|sh","|bash")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Container Web Service Spawning Interactive Shell
id: 7e1b8b22-7c11-4f2d-9b40-9a5a3e7e1a01
description: Detects redis-server, nginx, node, java, httpd or apache2 spawning sh/bash with download or staging command-line — classic post-exploit pattern for CVE-2025-49844 / CVE-2026-24061 inside containers.
references:
  - https://securelist.com/container-security-typical-issues/119974/
author: SOC
date: 2026/05/29
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1203
  - attack.t1059.004
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/redis-server'
      - '/nginx'
      - '/node'
      - '/java'
      - '/httpd'
      - '/apache2'
      - '/php-fpm'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - '/dash'
      - '/busybox'
      - '/ash'
      - '/zsh'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'curl '
      - 'wget '
      - '/tmp/'
      - '/dev/shm/'
      - 'chmod +x'
      - 'base64 -d'
      - 'bash -i'
      - '|sh'
      - '|bash'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
level: high
source:(linux.auditd OR windows.sysmon) @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.parent.name:(redis-server OR nginx OR node OR java OR httpd OR apache2 OR php-fpm) OR @ParentImage:(*\\redis-server* OR *\\nginx.exe OR *\\node.exe OR *\\java.exe)) @process.command_line:(*curl* OR *wget* OR *"/tmp/"* OR *"/dev/shm/"* OR *"chmod +x"* OR *"base64 -d"* OR *"bash -i"*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(redis-server|nginx|node|java|httpd|apache2|php-fpm)$/i
| ImageFileName=/\/(sh|bash|dash|busybox|ash|zsh)$/i
| regex("(curl |wget |/tmp/|/dev/shm/|chmod \\+x|base64 -d|bash -i|\\|sh|\\|bash)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("redis-server","nginx","node","java","httpd","apache2") Processes.process_name IN ("sh","bash","dash","busybox","ash") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(process, "(?i)(curl|wget|chmod|/tmp/|/dev/shm/|base64|nc |bash -i)") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("redis-server","nginx","node","java","httpd","apache2") Processes.process_name IN ("sh","bash","dash","busybox","ash") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(process, "(?i)(curl|wget|chmod|/tmp/|/dev/shm/|base64|nc |bash -i)") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
[LLM] Container privilege escalation via Looney Tunables, PwnKit, sudo chroot Exploitation High
Detects CVE-2023-4911 (GLIBC_TUNABLES env-var corruption), CVE-2021-4034 (pkexec PwnKit) and CVE-2025-32463 (sudo --chroot/-R) — the exact local-root chain named in the article for Kinsing and perfctl campaigns. Rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2023-4911 (Looney Tunables, Kinsing), CVE-2021-4034 (PwnKit, perfctl) and CVE-2025-32463 (sudo). Detection anchors on the unique exploit signatures — GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc. prefix is the Looney Tunables hallmark, sudo --chroot/-R is CVE-2025-32463-specific. Cross-checked against Qualys advisory for Looney Tunables and the sudo CVE-2025-32463 advisory. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.qualys.com/vulnerabilities-threat-research/2023/10/03/cve-2023-4911-looney-tunables-local-privilege-escalation-in-the-glibcs-ld-so • https://www.stratascale.com/vulnerability-alert-CVE-2025-32463-sudo-chroot • https://attack.mitre.org/software/S1180/
ATT&CKT1068 T1548.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (ProcessCommandLine has "GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.")
    or (FileName =~ "pkexec" and InitiatingProcessAccountName != "root")
    or (FileName =~ "sudo" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--chroot "," -R /","--chroot="," -R="))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where (ActingProcessCommandLine has "GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.")
    or (ActingProcessName endswith "/pkexec" and ActorUsername != "root")
    or (ActingProcessName endswith "/sudo" and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--chroot "," -R /","--chroot="," -R="))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Linux Local Privilege Escalation via Looney Tunables, PwnKit or sudo chroot
id: 4d3b9c2e-2f01-4a8e-b6ed-3e6f1e2c2b02
description: Detects the three local-root chains named in the Kaspersky container-security article — CVE-2023-4911 GLIBC_TUNABLES, CVE-2021-4034 pkexec PwnKit, CVE-2025-32463 sudo --chroot/-R.
references:
  - https://securelist.com/container-security-typical-issues/119974/
  - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2023-4911
  - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2021-4034
  - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-32463
author: SOC
date: 2026/05/29
tags:
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.t1548.003
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  sel_tunables:
    CommandLine|contains: 'GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.'
  sel_pkexec:
    Image|endswith: '/pkexec'
  sel_sudo:
    Image|endswith: '/sudo'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '--chroot '
      - ' -R /'
      - '--chroot='
  condition: sel_tunables or sel_pkexec or sel_sudo
level: high
source:linux.auditd (@process.command_line:*GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.* OR (@process.executable.path:*/pkexec AND -@user.name:root) OR (@process.executable.path:*/sudo AND @process.command_line:(*"--chroot "* OR *" -R /"*)))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| (CommandLine=/GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc\./
   OR (ImageFileName=/\/pkexec$/i AND UserName!="root")
   OR (ImageFileName=/\/sudo$/i AND CommandLine=/(--chroot |\s-R\s+\/|--chroot=)/))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process IN ("*GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.*","*pkexec*","*sudo --chroot*","*sudo -R *") OR Processes.process_name="pkexec") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process IN ("*GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.*","*pkexec*","*sudo --chroot*","*sudo -R *") OR Processes.process_name="pkexec") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
[LLM] perfctl rootkit — /etc/ld.so.preload write or LD_PRELOAD on root daemon Installation High
Hunts the perfctl userland rootkit footprint named in the article: write to /etc/ld.so.preload, or a long-running root daemon launched with LD_PRELOAD pointing at a non-standard library — both are the canonical Linux process-hiding persistence pattern. Rationale: Article explicitly states perfctl 'install a rootkit that hides the presence of perfctl on the system' after CVE-2021-4034. /etc/ld.so.preload and LD_PRELOAD are the canonical Linux userland rootkit primitives. Cross-checked against Aqua Nautilus perfctl write-up and MITRE T1574.006 page. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aquasec.com/blog/perfctl-a-stealthy-malware-targeting-millions-of-linux-servers/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1574/006/
ATT&CKT1014 T1574.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
union
(
  DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where FolderPath =~ "/etc/ld.so.preload" or FileName =~ "ld.so.preload"
  | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
),
(
  DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where ProcessCommandLine has "LD_PRELOAD="
  | where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/","LD_PRELOAD=/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/"))
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType="LD_PRELOAD_exec", FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName=InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName=AccountName
)
| order by Timestamp desc
union
(
  ImFileEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where TargetFilePath =~ "/etc/ld.so.preload"
  | where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, EventType, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
),
(
  ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "LD_PRELOAD="
  | where not (ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/","LD_PRELOAD=/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/"))
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname=DvcHostname, ActorUsername=ActorUsername, EventType="LD_PRELOAD_exec", TargetFilePath="", ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Write to /etc/ld.so.preload or Suspicious LD_PRELOAD on Root Daemon
id: 9c2f54a1-7d6c-4f0d-8a13-2b4f2e9c1d03
description: Detects the perfctl userland rootkit persistence pattern named in Kaspersky's container security analysis — modification of /etc/ld.so.preload or process launched with LD_PRELOAD pointing outside standard library paths.

[LLM] Container default credential leak — PKP_DB_PASSWORD=changeMePlease and --secret Weaponization Medium
Hunts the exact plaintext credential anti-patterns shown in the article's Dockerfile screenshots: PKP_DB_PASSWORD set to changeMePlease (or any default vendor value) baked into image layers, and processes launched with --secret <value> arguments visible in /proc. Rationale: Article's verbatim code blocks include PKP_DB_PASSWORD, changeMePlease and --secret as plaintext-credential examples (Block 1/2/3 in tables). The Phase 3 citation explicitly calls out passwords-on-command-line being visible in /proc. PKP_DB_PASSWORD is the documented OJS/PKP default — confirmed via PKP project docs. Cross-checked against: • https://docs.pkp.sfu.ca/admin-guide/en/deploy-docker • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/001/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.003 T1078.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("PKP_DB_PASSWORD=","=changeMePlease"," --secret ","MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=","POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres","REDIS_PASSWORD=redis")
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("vault","sops","kubectl"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("PKP_DB_PASSWORD=","=changeMePlease"," --secret ","MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=","POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres","REDIS_PASSWORD=redis")
| where not (ParentProcessName has_any ("vault","sops","kubectl"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'PKP_DB_PASSWORD='
      - '=changeMePlease'
      - ' --secret '
      - 'MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD='
      - 'POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres'
      - 'REDIS_PASSWORD=redis'
  filter_vault:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/vault'
      - '/sops'
      - '/kubectl'
  condition: selection and not filter_vault
level: medium
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.command_line:(*PKP_DB_PASSWORD=* OR *=changeMePlease* OR *" --secret "* OR *MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=* OR *POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres* OR *REDIS_PASSWORD=redis*) -@process.parent.name:(vault OR sops OR kubectl)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| CommandLine=/(PKP_DB_PASSWORD=|=changeMePlease|\s--secret\s|MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=|POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres|REDIS_PASSWORD=redis)/
| NOT ParentBaseFileName=/^(vault|sops|kubectl)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process IN ("*PKP_DB_PASSWORD=*","*=changeMePlease*","* --secret *","*MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=*","*POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process IN ("*PKP_DB_PASSWORD=*","*=changeMePlease*","* --secret *","*MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=*","*POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
[LLM] Container-to-container horizontal scan — Dero miner self-propagation Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects compromised containers fanning out to scan adjacent network ranges for additional vulnerable services, the article-described Dero miner self-propagation behaviour. Threshold-based: many unique destinations on a small set of vulnerable-service ports within a short window, sourced from a single container IP. Rationale: Article's Phase 6 citation describes Dero miner self-propagation via infected containers scanning for new targets. Port set chosen for the article-referenced vulnerable services: Redis (6379, CVE-2025-49844), Docker API (2375/2376), nginx-fronted apps (8080/9000), etcd (2379), DBs. cloudwatch_query left empty — container-to-container traffic does not naturally land in CloudWatch CloudTrail/VPC-flow trails in the analyst-pivot shape this UC needs. Cross-checked against Wiz Dero campaign write-up. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/dero-miner-attacks-on-kubernetes-clusters • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1046/
ATT&CKT1046 T1018
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where ActionType == "ConnectionAttempt" or ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| where RemotePort in (22, 2375, 2376, 6379, 8080, 9000, 9200, 2379, 5432, 3306)
| where RemoteIPType in ("Private","Public")
| summarize UniqueDests = dcount(RemoteIP), Ports = make_set(RemotePort, 10), SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
          by DeviceName, LocalIP, InitiatingProcessFileName, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
| where UniqueDests > 50
| order by UniqueDests desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where DstPortNumber in (22, 2375, 2376, 6379, 8080, 9000, 9200, 2379, 5432, 3306)
| summarize UniqueDests = dcount(DstIpAddr), Ports = make_set(DstPortNumber, 10)
          by DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where UniqueDests > 50
| order by UniqueDests desc
source:(windows.sysmon OR linux.auditd) @network.destination.port:(22 OR 2375 OR 2376 OR 6379 OR 8080 OR 9000 OR 9200 OR 2379 OR 5432 OR 3306)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4
| RemotePort=22 OR RemotePort=2375 OR RemotePort=2376 OR RemotePort=6379 OR RemotePort=8080 OR RemotePort=9000 OR RemotePort=9200 OR RemotePort=2379 OR RemotePort=5432 OR RemotePort=3306
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemotePort], function=count(field=RemoteAddressIP4, distinct=true, as=UniqueDests))
| UniqueDests > 50
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count dc(All_Traffic.dest) as unique_dests min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest_port IN (22,2375,2376,6379,8080,9000,9200,2379,5432,3306) by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest_port _time span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | where unique_dests > 50 | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count dc(All_Traffic.dest) as unique_dests min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest_port IN (22,2375,2376,6379,8080,9000,9200,2379,5432,3306) by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest_port _time span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | where unique_dests > 50 | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
[LLM] Container egress to cryptominer pool / Kinsing C2 Command & Control High
Detects post-compromise C2 from containers: outbound connections to Stratum mining-pool ports (3333/4444/5555/7777/14444) or to known Kinsing/perfctl/Dero infrastructure indicators, initiated from a container-resident process (curl/wget/xmrig/perfctl). Rationale: Article ties Kinsing/perfctl/Dero/Mirai/Gafgyt to compromised containers (Phase 8). Stratum port set is the documented mining-pool default for Monero/Dero. Domain indicators cross-checked against abuse.ch ThreatFox Kinsing entries and Aqua Nautilus perfctl/Dero write-ups. Cross-checked against: • https://threatfox.abuse.ch/browse/malware/win.kinsing/ • https://www.aquasec.com/blog/perfctl-a-stealthy-malware-targeting-millions-of-linux-servers/ • https://www.wiz.io/blog/dero-miner-attacks-on-kubernetes-clusters
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105 T1496
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
union
(
  DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(1d)
  | where RemotePort in (3333, 4444, 5555, 7777, 14444, 14433, 45700)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Signal="stratum_port"
),
(
  DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(1d)
  | where RemoteUrl has_any ("xmrig","kinsing","perfctl","derohe.org","dero-stratum","minexmr","supportxmr","nanopool","pool.minexmr")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Signal="miner_url"
)
| order by Timestamp desc
union
(
  ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
  | where DstPortNumber in (3333, 4444, 5555, 7777, 14444, 14433, 45700)
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, Signal="stratum_port"
),
(
  ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
  | where DnsQuery has_any ("xmrig","kinsing","perfctl","derohe.org","dero-stratum","minexmr","supportxmr","nanopool")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr="", DstPortNumber=0, Url=DnsQuery, Signal="miner_dns"
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-55182", "CVE-2023-4911", "CVE-2021-4034", "CVE-2025-49844", "CVE-2026-24061", "CVE-2025-32463", "CVE-2017-9841", "CVE-2023-33246")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-55182", "CVE-2023-4911", "CVE-2021-4034", "CVE-2025-49844", "CVE-2026-24061", "CVE-2025-32463", "CVE-2017-9841", "CVE-2023-33246")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2025-55182", "CVE-2023-4911", "CVE-2021-4034", "CVE-2025-49844", "CVE-2026-24061", "CVE-2025-32463", "CVE-2017-9841", "CVE-2023-33246")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2025-55182", "CVE-2023-4911", "CVE-2021-4034", "CVE-2025-49844", "CVE-2026-24061", "CVE-2025-32463", "CVE-2017-9841", "CVE-2023-33246")

RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard Installation High
ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.
ATT&CKT1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe")
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\atera_agent.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\SplashtopStreamer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\RustDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\NinjaOne.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT

    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Fake Webex camera-fix JSE dropper (fix-camera.jse) via wscript / mTSTCv8.mdxm · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Kimsuky Deploys HTTPSpy, Expands Arsenal with HelloDoor and VS Code Tunnels
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Kimsuky fake AhnLab/nProtect installer spawning regsvr32 with MemLoader.dll · [LLM] HTTPSpy loader-chain artifacts on disk (cacheMon.dat, engine.dat, spyInster.dll) · [LLM] MemLoader scheduled-task persistence after regsvr32 DLL load · Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] VS Code Remote Tunnel abuse for covert C2 (code tunnel) · [LLM] Kimsuky C2 callback to .r-e.kr / .o-r.kr / .n-e.kr dynamic-DNS infrastructure · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] AppleSeed GPKI directory enumeration / staging · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] Kimsuky fake AhnLab/nProtect installer spawning regsvr32 with MemLoader.dll Installation High
Detects the Kimsuky HTTPSpy installer chain where nos-setup.exe (fake nProtect Online Security) or astx-setup.exe (fake AhnLab Safe Transaction / ASTx) launches regsvr32.exe to side-load MemLoader.dll, the second-stage DLL that establishes scheduled-task persistence and beacons to C2. Rationale: Uses three article-specific strings together (parent binaries nos-setup.exe / astx-setup.exe + regsvr32 child + MemLoader.dll cmdline). All three named explicitly by ENKI as the Kimsuky HTTPSpy installer chain. Cross-checked against MITRE Kimsuky/G0094 and CrowdStrike's 2025 European Threat Landscape mention of HTTPSpy. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0094/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/kimsuky-deploys-httpspy-expands-arsenal.html

| where NewProcessName endswith "\\regsvr32.exe"

| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Fake Webex camera-fix JSE dropper (fix-camera.jse) via wscript / mTSTCv8.mdxm Delivery High
Detects the April 2026 Kimsuky Webex lure where the victim runs an encrypted JScript file fix-camera.jse via wscript/cscript, which uses PowerShell to drop the intermediate downloader mTSTCv8.mdxm before fetching engine.dat / spyInster.dll. Hunts for either the JSE file execution or the unusual .mdxm extension on disk. Rationale: The .mdxm extension is a non-standard Kimsuky-specific artifact named in the ENKI report; fix-camera.jse and mTSTCv8.mdxm are unique enough that any hit is high-fidelity. Combines the JSE delivery vector with the intermediate-downloader filename. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/kimsuky-deploys-httpspy-expands-arsenal.html • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0094/

[LLM] HTTPSpy loader-chain artifacts on disk (cacheMon.dat, engine.dat, spyInster.dll) Installation High
Detects creation of the unique Kimsuky HTTPSpy stage filenames - cacheMon.dat (loader), engine.dat / spyInster.dll (mid-stage DLLs), mTSTCv8.mdxm (intermediate downloader), MemLoader.dll (installer DLL), and fix-camera.jse - regardless of which entry vector dropped them. Rationale: These six filenames are HTTPSpy/Kimsuky-specific and unlikely to collide with anything benign (engine.dat is generic on its own but in combination with the other five becomes a strong cluster). Disk-write detection catches both the installer and Webex JSE chains in one rule. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/kimsuky-deploys-httpspy-expands-arsenal.html

[LLM] VS Code Remote Tunnel abuse for covert C2 (code tunnel) Command & Control Medium
Detects execution of Microsoft VS Code's Remote Tunneling feature (code.exe / code-tunnel.exe with the 'tunnel' subcommand) which Kaspersky observed Kimsuky abusing to establish covert C2 without traditional malware. Tunes for non-developer accounts on hosts that do not normally run VS Code. Rationale: Targets the specific 'code tunnel' invocation pattern Kaspersky documented as Kimsuky's TTP. Includes the --accept-server-license-terms / --random-name / serve-web args that distinguish the C2 use from a developer's normal VS Code launch. Also flagged by Darktrace and Logpresso per the article. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/kimsuky-deploys-httpspy-expands-arsenal.html • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1219/
ATT&CKT1219 T1102
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("code.exe","code-tunnel.exe","code-insiders.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "tunnel"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--accept-server-license-terms","--name","--random-name","serve-web"," tunnel ")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\code.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\code-tunnel.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\code-insiders.exe"
| where CommandLine has "tunnel"
| where CommandLine has_any ("--accept-server-license-terms","--name","--random-name","serve-web")
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] AppleSeed GPKI directory enumeration / staging Actions on Objectives High
Detects access, copy, or read of files under C:\GPKI - the South Korean Government Public Key Infrastructure certificate directory that the AppleSeed Spy variant (and Troll Stealer before it) specifically targets per Kaspersky's 2026 Kimsuky report. Excludes platform processes that legitimately enumerate the filesystem. Rationale: C:\GPKI is specifically named in the article (Kaspersky / Troll Stealer mirror) as the AppleSeed exfil target. Korean GPKI certificates are tied to government / enterprise identity and have no benign reason to be touched by non-platform processes. Cross-referenced with prior Troll Stealer reporting. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/kimsuky-deploys-httpspy-expands-arsenal.html • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0094/

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, PreviousFolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

| where not (ActingProcessName has_any ("explorer.exe","MsMpEng.exe","MsSense.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe","TrustedInstaller.exe"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, EventType, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Kimsuky C2 callback to .r-e.kr / .o-r.kr / .n-e.kr dynamic-DNS infrastructure Command & Control High
Detects DNS resolution or HTTPS callbacks to the Kimsuky 2026 campaign C2 set: eight explicit dynamic-DNS hostnames from ENKI plus the broader .r-e.kr / .o-r.kr / .n-e.kr TLD patterns the actor consistently uses. Both HTTPSpy and AppleSeed clusters use this infrastructure. Rationale: All eight FQDNs are ENKI-published Kimsuky 2026 C2 hosts. The .r-e.kr / .o-r.kr / .n-e.kr dynamic-DNS pattern is also documented as a Kimsuky staple by Kaspersky and CrowdStrike across multiple years, so the TLD-wide fallback catches future campaign rotation. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/kimsuky-deploys-httpspy-expands-arsenal.html • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0094/

[LLM] MemLoader scheduled-task persistence after regsvr32 DLL load Installation Medium
Detects the Kimsuky MemLoader persistence step where, after regsvr32 loads MemLoader.dll, a schtasks /create is issued to re-launch the DLL (often referencing regsvr32, the MemLoader path, or AppData/Public stage paths). Article states 'DLL establishes persistence on the host using a scheduled task'. Rationale: schtasks /create alone is too noisy; combining it with the article's specific stage-binary names (MemLoader, cacheMon, spyInster) plus the user-writable AppData/Public stage paths anchors the detection to the Kimsuky chain. Parent exclusion drops admin GUI-driven task creation. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/kimsuky-deploys-httpspy-expands-arsenal.html • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1053/005/
ATT&CKT1053.005 T1547
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "schtasks.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/create"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("regsvr32","MemLoader","cacheMon","spyInster","\\AppData\\","\\Public\\",".dll")
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("mmc.exe","taskschd.msc","trustedinstaller.exe","msiexec.exe"))
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\schtasks.exe"
| where CommandLine has "/create"
| where CommandLine has_any ("regsvr32","MemLoader","cacheMon","spyInster","\\AppData\\","\\Public\\",".dll")
| where ParentProcessName !endswith "\\mmc.exe" and ParentProcessName !endswith "\\TrustedInstaller.exe" and ParentProcessName !endswith "\\msiexec.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT

| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine

    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("995a0a49ae4b244928b3f67e2bfd7a6e", "52f1ff082e981cbdfd1f045c6021c63f", "9fe43e08c8f446554340f972dac8a68c", "8e15c4d4f71bdd9dbc48cd2cabc87806",         | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)

                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
—
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
